description: The bar chart illustrates the number of datasets related to hateful communication, categorized by the number of languages they include, across the years 2012 to 2021. The vertical axis, labeled "Number of datasets," uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10 to 100, while the horizontal axis represents the year. Two types of datasets are shown: those containing one language (blue bars) and those containing two or more languages (orange bars), as indicated by the legend. The data reveals a consistent increase in the total number of datasets over time. In the earlier years (2012–2015), the number of datasets was low, with only a few one-language datasets. From 2016 onwards, there is a significant rise, with the number of one-language datasets reaching approximately 13 in 2016 and peaking at over 100 in 2021. The number of two-or-more-language datasets begins to appear in 2017, with a noticeable increase in 2018 and 2019, peaking at around 20 in 2020 before declining slightly to about 10 in 2021. The chart also includes a light blue bar for 2021, which is not explained in the legend, and a grey bar for the same year, both of which are not accounted for in the legend.
